comments.author: Abel Radenac
comments.text:
R20 justification — engine adapter + backends (review round 2).

Chosen: keep Dagu a separate executable behind an `mtm/engine.py` adapter with
two backends (`docker` default, `host` explicit opt-in). The CLI never calls
Dagu directly; it builds argv and a `DockerRunner`/`LocalRunner` executes it.

Alternatives considered:
- Hard-wire host Dagu only: rejected — the default user path must need no host
  install, and the review asked the CLI to execute through the image.
- Embed Dagu's Go engine / reimplement a scheduler: rejected — GPL-3.0
  contamination plus duplicated retry/state logic; a subprocess keeps the
  boundary clean and the dependency auditable (decisions/0003).
- Shell the Dagu status text directly in commands.py: rejected — status parsing,
  dead-owner reconciliation and exit mapping are one concern and belong in one
  testable unit.

Maintenance trade-off: one extra indirection layer and a small status text
parser to keep in sync with Dagu 2.20.1; in exchange, the host vs docker choice
is a flag, the reconciliation logic is unit-tested offline, and swapping the
engine later touches one module.

comments.author: Abel Radenac
comments.text:
R20 justification — schemas/workflows shipped inside the package (review round 2).

Chosen: move `schemas/*.json` and `workflows/sample.yaml` under `mtm/` and ship
them as package data (`pyproject.toml` package-data), so an installed wheel still
validates configs and can render the sample DAG.

Alternatives considered:
- Keep them at repo root and resolve via a path relative to the checkout:
  rejected — an installed CLI would silently disable validation, which the review
  flagged as a correctness gap (a broken config would load as valid).
- Download the sample DAG at runtime: rejected — non-deterministic and contrary
  to the offline `verify`/reproducibility invariant.

Trade-off: package data adds a wheel-size and MANIFEST concern, covered by
`tests/test_packaging.py` which builds the wheel, asserts the two schemas and the
sample DAG are inside it, and runs the installed CLI from outside the source tree.

comments.author: Abel Radenac
comments.text:
R20 justification — bench ownership via `docker run --user`, no `chown -R`.

Chosen: the DockerRunner passes `--user <uid>:<gid>` so files written into the
bench-mounted state are owned by the invoking host user; the entrypoint no longer
chowns.

Alternatives considered:
- `chown -R` the bench in the entrypoint: rejected — the bench contains the
  immutable selected sources; recursively rewriting their ownership violates the
  "inputs are immutable" invariant and can silently alter an SDD-derived oracle's
  provenance.

Trade-off: the CLI must know the invoking uid/gid and the image must not depend on
running as root; in exchange no host file's ownership is ever mutated by a run.
`tests/test_engine.py` asserts the argv carries `--user` and never `chown`.

comments.author: Abel Radenac
comments.text:
R20 / review note — worklog vs Beads (reviewer's CLAUDE.md:12 clarification).

Both coexist on purpose: worklog holds fine detail of the agent's actions and
reasoning; Beads holds only what a PR reviewer needs. A little overlap is accepted.
Implementation choices are justified as Beads comments (comment_count on this issue
is now 3); the worklog is not a second backlog. The branch also re-synced main's
risk-register and R20 working rules into CLAUDE.md (merge), so it now carries both
the worklog rule and main's R20 rule.

comments.author: Abel Radenac
comments.text:
R20 justification — outcome taxonomy via a typed step marker (review round 3).

Chosen: a step types its own outcome by emitting an output variable
`MTM_CATEGORY` (values TEST_FINDING / INPUT_LIMITATION / TOOL), read from Dagu's
own run state. Untyped or unknown => tool/workflow failure (exit 30).

Alternatives: custom DAG step keys (rejected — Dagu's validator rejects unknown
keys); mapping Dagu exit/node status alone (rejected — the evidence is untyped,
which is the defect); a sidecar JSON file (deferred — the output variable already
rides a supported channel). Trade-off: verification steps must emit the marker
(PR 2/3 tooling will); in exchange the exit code is never invented from a generic
shell exit status. See worklog/decisions/0007.

comments.author: Abel Radenac
comments.text:
R20 justification — image build context is the source tree, not the wheel (round 3).

Chosen: keep `image/` in the source tree; `mtm install` requires a source context
and fails clearly (exit 40, CONFIG_INVALID) from an installed wheel. Tested from
outside a checkout.

Alternatives: package the whole Docker context in the wheel (rejected as
disproportionate — the Dockerfile copies `mtm/` and pyproject, and a wheel would
need to ship the full source tree, duplicating the distribution); make `install`
download a context (rejected — non-deterministic, breaks the offline invariant).
Trade-off: building the image needs a checkout; in exchange the wheel stays a
clean control CLI and the contract is explicit and tested. See worklog/decisions/0008.

comments.author: Abel Radenac
comments.text:
R20 justification — docker liveness via a run-id label; read-only bench mount (round 3).

Chosen: label the owner container `mtm.run-id=<id>` at run time; resolve liveness
with `docker ps --filter label=...`. Mount `<bench>:/bench:ro` and `<bench>/.mtm`
RW.

Alternatives: keep pid=0 -> INTERRUPTED (rejected — false interruption of live
runs); container PID via docker inspect (rejected — namespaced PID is not a
host-liveness signal); RW bench with RO seeds (rejected — the bench root *is* the
input tree). Trade-off: liveness assumes the same Docker context (a changed
context reads as "not found" => conservative INTERRUPTED); in exchange a running
run is never mislabelled and a run cannot overwrite immutable inputs.

comments.author: Abel Radenac
comments.text:
AP-01 acceptance evidence — PR1 feature gate (round 4). Local WSL, 2026-10-17,
head f4030b6 with main (AP-01) merged. Every applicable PR1 criterion mapped to an
executed command/test and its observed result:

1. CLI bootstrap with no GUI/manual installs beyond Docker
   -> `mtm init .` / `mtm doctor` (Docker 29.9.0; image present; credentials 600;
      host-cc ok) -> doctor SUCCEEDED. test_cli.py (init/scope/status/doctor).
2. Default workflow runs THROUGH THE CLI in the versioned Docker image, no host Dagu
   -> `mtm workflow run --run-id ap01-ok2` -> SUCCEEDED, exit 0, backend=docker.
      test_run_success_via_cli; test_docker_backend_does_not_require_host_dagu.
3. Textual DAG view -> `mtm workflow view` -> 3 ordered steps with `after:` edges.
4. Injected tool failure diagnosed accurately (exit 30, not a finding)
   -> step `exit 3` -> FAILED / TOOL / TOOL_FAILED / exit 30, cause names `boom`.
      Contrast: MTM_CATEGORY=TEST_FINDING -> exit 10; mixed finding+crash -> 30.
5. Failure visible in text `mtm status`, consulted twice
   -> after a failed run the text status prints last op stage/status/code/cause/
      action both times; a SUCCEEDED consultation does not overwrite the journal.
6. Kill/restart reconciles to INTERRUPTED, not success
   -> killed owner -> INTERRUPTED / owner_alive=False / exit 130.
      Contrast: live container -> RUNNING / owner_alive=True / exit 0 /
      OPERATION_RUNNING.
7. Selected-source read-only hashes preserved
   -> test_run_cannot_write_a_selected_source: injected write step actually runs
      and fails because the mount is read-only; bytes unchanged. CI repeats it.
8. Docker image delete/recreate
   -> `docker rmi utest-machinery/mtm:1.0.0` then `mtm install` -> SUCCEEDED,
      rebuilt from the packaged context with no source checkout.
9. Standalone install from a wheel (no checkout)
   -> wheel carries mtm/image/{Dockerfile,entrypoint.sh,toolchain.lock}; installed
      CLI resolves the packaged context. Packaging failures now FAIL (not skip)
      when the environment supports them.
10. Bench-scoped owner identity (two-bench collision)
   -> mtm.owner carries bench-<hash>__<run-id>; a same-named run in another bench
      reads not-alive (test_bench_scoped_label_avoids_cross_bench_collision).
11. Beads recovery from a fresh clone
   -> .beads/issues.jsonl exported in the PR; `bd prime`/`bd show utm-bu8` from it.
      Full Dolt sync per the pinned version's docs (JSONL is NOT a backup).
12. All local checks reproducible
   -> `python3 -m pytest` -> 71 passed, 1 skipped (opt-in host-Dagu).
      `python3 scripts/validate_baseline.py` -> PASS.

NOT_DEMONSTRATED (outside PR1 scope): real LLM/DeepSeek call (PR2), Mull/fuzz
(PR4), full SYS/QD qualification (PR6). R20: no new glue this round.

acceptance_criteria: A fresh selected C/SDD fixture becomes an executable unit suite; intentional defect detected; unknown oracle stays UNDETERMINED; no original modifications, no silent oracle weakening, no secret leak.

title: PR 3 — Offline deterministic verification
description: mtm verify rebuilds/runs the frozen bench without LLM, with independent functional/robustness, LLVM coverage/MC-DC, ASan/UBSan, optional LSan, GCC/Clang optimization and Valgrind profiles, each reporting applicability and limits.
acceptance_criteria: Offline replay works; execution, SDD applicability and tool failure are distinct; metrics match native tools; STALE_INPUT on changed inputs; no MCU timing assertions.

title: PR 4 — Mutation and generative robustness
description: Integrate Mull (matching LLVM) for non-destructive mutation/statuses and libFuzzer with properties, budget, corpus and reproducible crash inputs, reusing existing scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Native results preserved with correct denominators and survivor/invalid/equivalent statuses; no custom coverage/mutation engine; bounded repeatable fuzz scenarios.

title: PR 6 — Maintain and qualify the finished product
description: Incremental add/remove scope, source/SDD change impact, stable IDs/oracle approval, collaboration from clean checkout, complete C/SDD and product qualification, release/install/update guidance.
acceptance_criteria: All mandatory SYS/QD checks have recorded evidence; no critical unanswered defects; historical evidence persists; product installable and operable per user guide.

title: PR 5 — Explainable consolidated report
description: Deterministically aggregate native outputs into requirement <-> function <-> plan <-> test <-> execution <-> evidence; mtm interpret uses the in-image LLM on frozen evidence; mtm report renders linked HTML/JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Actions specify why, where, suggested fix, impact and reproduction; unknown never falsely PASS; interpret never changes raw results; HTML audit navigation works.
